summary: Create the OAuth app yourself in a few minutes. Organizations may need an owner to approve it.

verdict.label: Self-serve, about 30 min
verdict.wait: None for your own account; org owners may need to approve it
verdict.reason: You register the app in your own settings and it works right away. No review by GitHub is needed.

steps.title: Open the OAuth app settings
steps.detail: In GitHub go to Settings, Developer settings, OAuth Apps, then New OAuth App. If you have never created an app, the button reads Register a new application.

steps.title: Fill in the app details
steps.detail: Enter the application name, your homepage URL and the authorization callback URL where users return after login (you can add up to 10). A description and Device Flow are optional. Expire user access tokens is on by default; turn it off only if your auth code cannot handle short-lived tokens. Then click Register application.

steps.title: Save the client ID and generate a client secret
steps.detail: Store the secret in your secrets manager, never in code.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Request the smallest scopes you need, since scopes limit what a token can access. An agent can draft the scope list from your use case.

steps.title: Test with your own account
steps.detail: Run the login flow once and confirm you receive a token with the scopes you asked for.

blockers.title: Organization access restrictions
blockers.detail: Orgs can restrict third-party OAuth apps. When restrictions are on, members and outside collaborators must request approval from an org owner before they can authorize your app, and until it is approved the app can reach only the org's public resources. Orgs without restrictions authorize it automatically.
blockers.what_to_do: Tell the user to ask an org owner to approve the app. Owners do this under the org's OAuth app policy (Third-party Access, then Review, then Grant access).

blockers.title: OAuth App or GitHub App
blockers.detail: GitHub Apps have targeted permissions and GitHub recommends them over OAuth apps in general. OAuth apps use broad scopes. Picking the wrong type means redoing setup later.
blockers.what_to_do: Decide before building. Check which one your integration platform expects.
